teach.title: Domain and range
text: The domain is every x-value (input) a function can use. The range is every y-value (output) it produces.
On a graph, the domain is how far left to right the graph goes. The range is how far down to up it goes.

example.problem: A graph runs from x = −2 to x = 5 and from y = 0 to y = 9, with solid dots at every end. Find the domain and range.
steps: Left to right: x goes from −2 to 5, so the domain is −2 to 5.
Bottom to top: y goes from 0 to 9, so the range is 0 to 9.

teach.title: Interval notation
text: Use [ ] when the end value is included. Use ( ) when it is not included.
Infinity is never a real number, so ∞ and −∞ always get a parenthesis.

example.problem: Write −2 < x ≤ 5 in interval notation.
steps: −2 is not included, so use a parenthesis on the left: (−2.
5 is included, so use a bracket on the right: 5].

questions.prompt: The domain of a function is the set of all...
questions.hint: Which variable is the input?
questions.solution: The domain is every input, so it is the set of x-values. The range is the set of y-values.

questions.prompt: Write x ≥ 3 in interval notation.
questions.hint: Is 3 included? Does the interval go to the right or left?
questions.solution: x ≥ 3 includes 3, so use a bracket. It runs up forever to the right, and ∞ gets a parenthesis: [3, ∞).

questions.prompt: Write −2 < x ≤ 5 in interval notation.
questions.hint: < leaves the number out. ≤ keeps it in.
questions.solution: −2 is not included, so (−2. 5 is included, so 5]. Answer: (−2, 5].

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x² − 4. What is the smallest y-value on the graph?
questions.hint: Find the lowest point of the curve.
questions.solution: The lowest point of the parabola is its vertex, (0, −4). So the smallest y-value is −4.

questions.prompt: The graph of y = 2x − 1 is a line that goes on forever in both directions. What is its domain?
questions.hint: A line never stops going left or right.
questions.solution: The line extends forever left and right, so every x-value works. The domain is (−∞, ∞).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = √(x + 2). What is the smallest x-value on the graph?
questions.hint: Find where the curve starts on the left.
questions.solution: The graph starts at the point (−2, 0) and goes right from there. The smallest x-value is −2.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = √(x + 2). What is its range?
questions.hint: The range is about y-values. Where does the curve start vertically, and does it go up or down?
questions.solution: The curve starts at y = 0 and rises forever. The point (−2, 0) is on the graph, so 0 is included. Range: [0, ∞).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −x² + 3. What is its range?
questions.hint: The parabola opens down. Find its highest point.
questions.solution: The vertex (0, 3) is the highest point. All y-values are 3 or less, so the range is (−∞, 3].

teach.title: Domain from an equation
text: Two things break a function: dividing by zero and taking an even root (like a square root) of a negative number.
If neither happens, the domain is all real numbers. Otherwise, find the x-values that cause trouble and leave them out.

example.problem: Find the domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 3).
steps: The bottom cannot be 0: x − 3 = 0 when x = 3.
So every x except 3 is allowed.

teach.title: Range of simple functions
text: For a parabola, find the vertex. If it opens up, the vertex is the lowest point. If it opens down, the vertex is the highest point.

example.problem: Find the range of f(x) = x² + 1.
steps: x² is never negative, so its smallest value is 0.

questions.prompt: Which function has a domain of all real numbers?
questions.hint: Look for a function with no fraction and no square root.
questions.solution: A polynomial like 3x² − 5 has no division and no root, so every x works. The others have restrictions.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 1/(x − 4). Which x-value is not allowed?
questions.hint: Set the bottom equal to 0.
questions.solution: The bottom is 0 when x − 4 = 0, so x = 4. That value is not allowed.

questions.prompt: f(x) = √(x − 6). What is the smallest x-value allowed?
questions.hint: The inside of a square root cannot be negative: x − 6 ≥ 0.
questions.solution: Solve x − 6 ≥ 0 to get x ≥ 6. The smallest allowed value is 6.

questions.prompt: Find the domain of f(x) = √(x + 3).
questions.hint: Solve x + 3 ≥ 0.
questions.solution: x + 3 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ −3. At x = −3 the root is √0 = 0, which is fine, so use a bracket. Domain: [−3, ∞).

questions.prompt: Find the domain of f(x) = 1/(x + 5).
questions.hint: The bottom is 0 when x + 5 = 0.
questions.solution: x + 5 = 0 at x = −5, so −5 is the only excluded value. Domain: (−∞, −5) ∪ (−5, ∞).

questions.prompt: f(x) = √(2x − 10). What is the smallest x-value allowed?
questions.hint: Solve 2x − 10 ≥ 0.
questions.solution: 2x − 10 ≥ 0 gives 2x ≥ 10, so x ≥ 5. The smallest x is 5.

questions.prompt: Find the range of f(x) = x² + 3.
questions.hint: The vertex is the lowest point of a parabola that opens up.
questions.solution: x² is at least 0, so x² + 3 is at least 3. The vertex (0, 3) is on the graph. Range: [3, ∞).

questions.prompt: Find the range of f(x) = −x² + 7.
questions.hint: The negative in front makes the parabola open down.
questions.solution: −x² is at most 0, so −x² + 7 is at most 7. The vertex (0, 7) is the highest point. Range: (−∞, 7].

questions.prompt: How many x-values are not allowed in the domain of f(x) = 5/(x² − 9)?
questions.hint: Solve x² − 9 = 0.
questions.solution: x² − 9 = 0 gives x = 3 or x = −3. Two values are excluded.

teach.title: Intercepts
text: The y-intercept is where the graph crosses the y-axis. Set x = 0 and find f(0). It is the point (0, f(0)).
An x-intercept is where the graph crosses the x-axis. Set f(x) = 0 and solve for x. It is a point (x, 0).

example.problem: Find the intercepts of f(x) = 2x² − 8.
steps: x-intercepts: 2x² − 8 = 0, so x² = 4 and x = 2 or x = −2.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of f(x) = 3x − 6?
questions.hint: Set x = 0.
questions.solution: f(0) = 3(0) − 6 = −6. The y-intercept is (0, −6).

questions.prompt: The y-intercept of f(x) = x² − 5x + 8 is (0, k). What is k?
questions.hint: Find f(0).

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercept of f(x) = 2x + 10. Give the x-value.
questions.hint: Set f(x) = 0.

questions.prompt: What are the x-intercepts of f(x) = x² − 9?
questions.hint: Set x² − 9 = 0. An x-intercept has y = 0.
questions.solution: x² = 9, so x = 3 or x = −3. The points are (−3, 0) and (3, 0).

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of f(x) = x² − x − 6. Give the x-values.
questions.hint: Factor into two binomials.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x² + 2x − 3. What are its x-intercepts?
questions.hint: Find where the curve crosses the horizontal axis.
questions.solution: The curve crosses the x-axis at x = −3 and x = 1. Check: (x + 3)(x − 1) = x² + 2x − 3. The points are (−3, 0) and (1, 0).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = 2x − 4. At what x-value does the line cross the x-axis?
questions.hint: Find where y = 0.
questions.solution: Set 2x − 4 = 0, so x = 2. The line crosses the x-axis at (2, 0).

questions.prompt: How many x-intercepts does f(x) = x² + 4 have?
questions.hint: Try solving x² + 4 = 0. Can a square equal −4?
questions.solution: x² + 4 = 0 gives x² = −4, which has no real solution. The graph never touches the x-axis, so it has 0 x-intercepts.

teach.title: Putting it together
text: For one function you can often find the domain, range, and intercepts. Take them one at a time.
Domain: look for division and even roots. Range: think about the lowest or highest point. Intercepts: set x = 0 for y, and set f(x) = 0 for x.

example.problem: For f(x) = √(x + 3) − 1, find the domain, range, and x-intercept.
steps: Range: √(x + 3) is at least 0, so f(x) is at least −1. Range: [−1, ∞).
x-intercept: √(x + 3) − 1 = 0, so √(x + 3) = 1, so x + 3 = 1 and x = −2. The point is (−2, 0).

questions.prompt: Find the domain and range of f(x) = √(x − 1) + 2.
questions.hint: Domain comes from x − 1 ≥ 0. The root part is at least 0, then add 2.
questions.solution: x − 1 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ 1, so the domain is [1, ∞). √(x − 1) ≥ 0, so f(x) ≥ 2 and the range is [2, ∞).

questions.prompt: Find the domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 3).
questions.hint: What x-value makes the bottom 0?
questions.solution: x − 3 = 0 at x = 3. So x = 3 is the only excluded value. Domain: (−∞, 3) ∪ (3, ∞).

questions.prompt: f(x) = √(12 − 3x). What is the largest x-value allowed?
questions.hint: Solve 12 − 3x ≥ 0. Dividing by a negative flips the inequality.
questions.solution: 12 − 3x ≥ 0 gives −3x ≥ −12, so x ≤ 4. The largest allowed x is 4.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −x² + 4x. What is its range?
questions.hint: The parabola opens down. Find the y-value of its highest point.
questions.solution: The vertex is at x = 2, and y = −4 + 8 = 4. The graph opens down, so the range is (−∞, 4].

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −x² + 4x. Where does it cross the x-axis? Give both x-values.
questions.hint: Read the two points where the curve meets the x-axis.
questions.solution: Set −x² + 4x = 0, so −x(x − 4) = 0. Then x = 0 or x = 4.

questions.prompt: f(x) = (x + 2)(x − 5). What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept?
questions.hint: Find f(0).

questions.prompt: Which interval notation matches −1 < x ≤ 6?
questions.hint: Check each end separately.
questions.solution: −1 is not included: (−1. 6 is included: 6]. Answer: (−1, 6].

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = √(x + 4) − 3. What is the y-coordinate of its y-intercept?
questions.hint: Find f(0).

questions.prompt: Find the x-values excluded from the domain of f(x) = 6/(x² − 16).
questions.hint: Solve x² − 16 = 0.
questions.solution: x² = 16, so x = 4 or x = −4. Both make the bottom 0.

teach.title: Increasing and decreasing
text: Read a graph from left to right. If it goes uphill, the function is increasing. If it goes downhill, it is decreasing.
Write intervals using x-values, in interval notation. Use parentheses: the function is not increasing or decreasing at the exact turning point.

example.problem: A parabola has vertex (3, −2) and opens up. Where is it increasing and decreasing?
steps: To the left of x = 3 the graph goes downhill: decreasing on (−∞, 3).
To the right of x = 3 it goes uphill: increasing on (3, ∞).

questions.prompt: Reading a graph from left to right, it goes uphill. The function is...
questions.hint: Think of walking along the graph from left to right.
questions.solution: Uphill from left to right means the y-values grow as x grows. That is increasing.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = (x − 2)² − 1. On which interval is it decreasing?
questions.hint: Intervals use x-values. Where does the graph go downhill?
questions.solution: The vertex is (2, −1). To the left of x = 2 the graph falls. It is decreasing on (−∞, 2).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = (x − 2)² − 1. On which interval is it increasing?
questions.hint: The graph goes uphill after the vertex.
questions.solution: To the right of the vertex x = 2 the graph rises. It is increasing on (2, ∞).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = (x − 2)² − 1. At what x-value does it switch from decreasing to increasing?
questions.hint: Find the x-coordinate of the lowest point.
questions.solution: The switch happens at the vertex (2, −1). The x-value is 2.

questions.prompt: The graph of f(x) = −2x + 3 is a line. Which statement is true?
questions.hint: Is the slope positive or negative?
questions.solution: The slope is −2, so the line falls from left to right everywhere. It is decreasing on (−∞, ∞).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −(x + 1)² + 4. At what x-value does it turn around?
questions.hint: Find the x-coordinate of the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex is (−1, 4). It turns at x = −1.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −(x + 1)² + 4. On which interval is it increasing?
questions.hint: This parabola opens down. Which side of the vertex goes uphill?
questions.solution: It opens down, so it rises on the left of the vertex x = −1. Increasing on (−∞, −1).

questions.prompt: Which function is increasing for all x?
questions.hint: Look for a positive slope.
questions.solution: Only 2x − 7 has a positive slope. −3x + 1 decreases, x² turns around at 0, and 5 is constant.

teach.title: Maximum and minimum
text: A relative maximum is a peak: the graph rises, then falls. A relative minimum is a valley: it falls, then rises.
The value is the y-coordinate. The place where it happens is the x-coordinate. Read each one carefully.

example.problem: A graph has a peak at (−1, 2). State the maximum value and where it occurs.
steps: The value is the y-coordinate: the maximum value is 2.
It occurs at the x-coordinate: x = −1.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x. On which intervals is it increasing?
questions.hint: Find the two turning points, then see where the graph goes uphill.
questions.solution: The graph rises up to x = −1, falls between x = −1 and x = 1, then rises again. It is increasing on (−∞, −1) and (1, ∞).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x. On which interval is it decreasing?
questions.hint: Where does the graph go downhill?
questions.solution: The graph goes downhill between its two turning points, x = −1 and x = 1. Decreasing on (−1, 1).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x. What is the relative maximum value?
questions.hint: The peak is the left turning point. Read its y-coordinate.
questions.solution: The peak is at (−1, 2). The maximum value is its y-coordinate, 2.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x. What is the relative minimum value?
questions.hint: The valley is the right turning point.
questions.solution: The valley is at (1, −2). The minimum value is its y-coordinate, −2.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x. At what x-value does the relative maximum occur?
questions.hint: The x-value is where it happens, not the height.
questions.solution: The peak is at (−1, 2). It occurs at x = −1.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x² − 6x + 5. Which statement is correct?
questions.hint: Find the vertex. The value is y, and where it occurs is x.
questions.solution: The vertex is (3, −4). The parabola opens up, so it is a minimum. The value is −4 and it occurs at x = 3.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −x² + 2x + 3. What is its maximum value?
questions.hint: Find the y-coordinate of the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex is (1, 4) because f(1) = −1 + 2 + 3 = 4. The maximum value is 4.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of f(x) = (x − 4)² + 7?
questions.hint: Vertex form shows the vertex directly.
questions.solution: The vertex is (4, 7) and the parabola opens up. The minimum value is 7.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum of f(x) = −(x + 2)² + 9?
questions.hint: Read the vertex (h, k) from the form a(x − h)² + k.
questions.solution: The vertex is (−2, 9). The parabola opens down, so the vertex is the maximum. Value 9 at x = −2.

teach.title: End behavior
text: End behavior says where the graph goes at the far left and far right. We write x → ∞ (far right) and x → −∞ (far left).

For a polynomial, look at the leading term. Even degree: both ends go the same way. Odd degree: the ends go opposite ways. A positive leading coefficient means the right end goes up. A negative one means the right end goes down.

example.problem: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = −2x³ + 5x.
steps: The leading term is −2x³: odd degree, negative coefficient.
Odd degree means opposite ends. Negative means the right end goes down.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x³. Which describes its end behavior?
choices: Rises to both the left and right
Falls to the left, rises to the right
Falls to both the left and right
Rises to the left, falls to the right
questions.hint: Check the far left and the far right of the curve.
questions.solution: On the left the graph goes down. On the right it goes up. Falls to the left, rises to the right.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −x³ + 2x. Which describes its end behavior?
choices: Rises to the left, falls to the right
Falls to the left, rises to the right
Rises to both the left and right
Falls to both the left and right
questions.hint: Look at both ends of the graph.
questions.solution: The left end is high and the right end is low. Rises to the left, falls to the right.

questions.prompt: What is the degree of f(x) = −3x⁴ + x²?
questions.hint: The degree is the highest exponent.
questions.solution: The highest exponent is 4, so the degree is 4.

questions.prompt: What is the leading coefficient of f(x) = 5x − 2x³ + 1?
questions.hint: Write the terms from highest power to lowest first.
questions.solution: In order: −2x³ + 5x + 1. The leading term is −2x³, so the leading coefficient is −2.

questions.prompt: Which describes the end behavior of f(x) = −3x⁴ + x²?
questions.hint: Even degree, negative leading coefficient.
questions.solution: The degree 4 is even, so both ends match. The coefficient −3 is negative, so both ends go down.

questions.prompt: Which describes the end behavior of f(x) = 2x³ − x?
questions.hint: Odd degree, positive leading coefficient.
questions.solution: Degree 3 is odd, so the ends go opposite ways. The coefficient 2 is positive, so the right end goes up and the left end goes down.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 3x². Which describes its end behavior?
choices: Falls to both the left and right
Rises to both the left and right
Falls to the left, rises to the right
Rises to the left, falls to the right
questions.hint: Ignore the bumps in the middle. Look at the far ends.
questions.solution: Both far ends of the graph go up. This matches degree 4 with a positive leading coefficient.

questions.prompt: A polynomial graph falls to the left and rises to the right. Is its degree even or odd? Type even or odd.
questions.hint: Even degrees have both ends going the same way.
questions.solution: The ends go in opposite directions, so the degree is odd.

questions.prompt: Which describes the end behavior of f(x) = −x⁵ + 3x²?
questions.hint: Degree 5 is odd. The leading coefficient is −1.
questions.solution: Odd degree gives opposite ends. The negative coefficient sends the right end down, so the left end goes up.

teach.title: Using all the features
text: One graph can give you intervals of increase and decrease, relative maximums and minimums, and end behavior. Describe them in order.
The function is increasing or decreasing between turning points. Turning points are exactly where maximums and minimums happen.

example.problem: A parabola opens down with vertex (4, 9). Describe it.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 2x². On which intervals is it decreasing?
questions.hint: The graph has two valleys and one peak in between.
questions.solution: The graph falls until the valley at x = −1, rises to the peak at x = 0, falls to the valley at x = 1, then rises. Decreasing on (−∞, −1) and (0, 1).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 2x². On which intervals is it increasing?
questions.hint: Find the intervals between the valleys and the peak where the graph climbs.
questions.solution: The graph rises from the left valley (x = −1) to the peak (x = 0), and from the right valley (x = 1) onward. Increasing on (−1, 0) and (1, ∞).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 2x². What is the lowest y-value on the graph?
questions.hint: Read the y-coordinate of either valley.
questions.solution: Both valleys are at y = −1, for example the point (1, −1). The lowest y-value is −1.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 2x². What is the y-value of the peak between the two valleys?
questions.hint: The peak is on the y-axis.
questions.solution: The peak is at (0, 0). Its value is 0.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = x⁴ − 2x². Which describes its end behavior?
choices: Falls to both the left and right
Rises to both the left and right
Falls to the left, rises to the right
Rises to the left, falls to the right
questions.hint: The degree is 4 and the leading coefficient is 1.
questions.solution: Even degree means both ends match. The positive coefficient means both go up.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown so its height in feet is h(t) = −16t² + 64t, where t is in seconds. At what time is the ball highest?
questions.hint: The vertex has x = −b/(2a).

questions.prompt: For h(t) = −16t² + 64t, what is the ball's maximum height in feet?
questions.hint: Plug the time of the vertex into h(t). The vertex is at t = 2.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = −x³ + 3x. On which interval is it increasing?
questions.hint: Look at the end behavior first: the leading coefficient is negative.
questions.solution: With a negative leading coefficient the left end is high and goes down first. It falls on (−∞, −1), rises on (−1, 1) between the valley (−1, −2) and peak (1, 2), then falls on (1, ∞). Increasing on (−1, 1).

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of f(x) = x² − 4x + 3?
questions.hint: Find the vertex first: x = −b/(2a).
questions.solution: x = 4/2 = 2. f(2) = 4 − 8 + 3 = −1. The minimum value is −1.

teach.title: Linear, quadratic, cubic, absolute value
text: A parent function is the simplest version of a function family. Every other function in the family is a transformation of it.
Linear f(x) = x: a straight line. Quadratic f(x) = x²: a U-shaped parabola. Cubic f(x) = x³: an S-shaped curve. Absolute value f(x) = |x|: a V with its corner at (0, 0).

example.problem: Complete a table for f(x) = x² at x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2.
steps: The values are 4, 1, 0, 1, 4. They are symmetric, which is typical for a parabola.

questions.prompt: Which equation is the parent quadratic function?
questions.hint: Quadratic means the highest power is 2.
questions.solution: Quadratic functions have an x². The parent is f(x) = x².

questions.prompt: This graph has an S-bend at the origin. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: It has an S shape and passes through the origin.
questions.solution: The graph rises from low left to high right with a flat S-bend at the origin. That is the cubic f(x) = x³.

questions.prompt: This graph is a V with a sharp corner. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: The graph has a sharp corner, not a smooth curve.
questions.solution: A V with a sharp corner at the origin is the absolute value function f(x) = |x|.

questions.prompt: This graph is a straight line through the origin. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: There is no bend at all.
questions.solution: A straight line through the origin with slope 1 is the linear parent function f(x) = x.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x². Find f(−3).
questions.hint: Square −3. A negative squared is positive.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x³. Find f(−2).
questions.hint: Cube means multiply three times.

questions.prompt: f(x) = |x|. Find f(−7).
questions.hint: Absolute value is the distance from 0.

questions.prompt: A table shows x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and f(x) = 4, 1, 0, 1, 4. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: Compare with x² and |x|.
questions.solution: x² gives 4, 1, 0, 1, 4. |x| would give 2, 1, 0, 1, 2. So it is quadratic.

questions.prompt: A table shows x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and f(x) = −8, −1, 0, 1, 8. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: Notice the outputs are negative for negative x.
questions.solution: x³ gives −8, −1, 0, 1, 8. This is the cubic.

teach.title: Square root, cube root, reciprocal, exponential
text: Square root f(x) = √x starts at the origin and curves to the right. Cube root f(x) = ∛x is like a sideways S through the origin.
Reciprocal f(x) = 1/x has two separate branches and never touches either axis. Exponential f(x) = 2ˣ climbs quickly on the right and flattens toward 0 on the left.

example.problem: Evaluate f(x) = ∛x at x = −8.

questions.prompt: This graph starts at the origin and curves to the right. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: It begins at a point and goes only to the right.
questions.solution: The curve starts at (0, 0) and goes right. That is f(x) = √x.

questions.prompt: This graph is a sideways S that is steep at the origin and flattens out far from it. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: It passes through the origin and goes both left and right.
questions.solution: It goes through (−8, −2), (0, 0), and (8, 2) like a sideways S. That is f(x) = ∛x.

questions.prompt: This graph has two separate branches. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: It has two separate pieces.
questions.solution: Two branches that never touch the axes make the reciprocal function f(x) = 1/x.

questions.prompt: This graph crosses the y-axis at (0, 1) and climbs fast. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: It never goes below the x-axis and grows faster and faster.
questions.solution: The curve crosses the y-axis at (0, 1) and climbs quickly. That is f(x) = 2ˣ.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2ˣ. Find f(5).
questions.hint: Multiply 2 by itself 5 times.

questions.prompt: f(x) = √x. Find f(49).
questions.hint: What number times itself is 49?

questions.prompt: f(x) = ∛x. Find f(−27).
questions.hint: What number cubed is −27?

questions.prompt: f(x) = 1/x. Find f(4).
questions.hint: The reciprocal of 4 is 1 over 4.

questions.prompt: Which parent function has a graph made of two separate branches?
questions.hint: One function cannot use x = 0.
questions.solution: Because x = 0 is not allowed, the graph of 1/x breaks into a piece on each side of the y-axis.

teach.title: Domain and range of the parent functions
text: Linear, cubic, and cube root: domain (−∞, ∞), range (−∞, ∞).
Quadratic and absolute value: domain (−∞, ∞), range [0, ∞). Square root: domain [0, ∞), range [0, ∞).
Reciprocal: both domain and range are (−∞, 0) ∪ (0, ∞). Exponential 2ˣ: domain (−∞, ∞), range (0, ∞).

example.problem: Give the domain and range of f(x) = √x.
steps: You cannot take the square root of a negative, so x ≥ 0. Domain: [0, ∞).
The root is never negative, and it reaches 0. Range: [0, ∞).

questions.prompt: What is the domain of f(x) = √x?
questions.hint: Negative numbers have no real square root.
questions.solution: Only x ≥ 0 works, and 0 is included. Domain: [0, ∞).

questions.prompt: What is the range of f(x) = x²?
questions.hint: A square is never negative, but it can be 0.
questions.solution: x² ≥ 0 and x = 0 gives 0. Range: [0, ∞).

questions.prompt: What is the domain of f(x) = 1/x?
questions.hint: Which input would divide by zero?
questions.solution: x = 0 is not allowed. Domain: (−∞, 0) ∪ (0, ∞).

questions.prompt: What is the range of f(x) = 2ˣ?
questions.hint: Can a power of 2 ever equal 0?
questions.solution: 2ˣ is always positive but never reaches 0. Range: (0, ∞).

questions.prompt: Which x-value is excluded from the domain of f(x) = 1/x?
questions.hint: Where would the bottom be zero?
questions.solution: The bottom is 0 when x = 0, so 0 is excluded.

questions.prompt: Which parent function has domain [0, ∞) and range [0, ∞)?
questions.hint: Both the inputs and outputs must be 0 or more.
questions.solution: Only the square root function has x ≥ 0 as its domain and y ≥ 0 as its range. x² and |x| allow negative x.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. What is the range of f(x) = |x|?
questions.hint: Read the lowest and highest y-values.
questions.solution: The V opens up from (0, 0). The y-values are 0 and larger. Range: [0, ∞).

questions.prompt: As x gets more and more negative, 2ˣ gets close to what number?
questions.solution: 2⁻¹ = 1/2, 2⁻² = 1/4, 2⁻³ = 1/8. The values shrink toward 0.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = ∛x. What are its domain and range?
questions.hint: Can you cube-root negative numbers?
questions.solution: You can take a cube root of any real number, and the outputs cover every number too. Both are (−∞, ∞).

teach.title: Even and odd functions
text: Even: f(−x) = f(x). The graph is symmetric about the y-axis, like a mirror. Examples: x², |x|.
Odd: f(−x) = −f(x). The graph is symmetric about the origin: spin it 180° and it looks the same. Examples: x, x³, ∛x, 1/x.
Neither: √x and 2ˣ.

example.problem: Is f(x) = x³ even or odd?
steps: That equals −f(x), so f is odd.

questions.prompt: Which parent function is even?
questions.hint: Even means f(−x) = f(x). Try x = 2 and x = −2.
questions.solution: |−2| = |2| = 2, so |x| is even. The others give opposite values for −2 and 2.

questions.prompt: Which parent function is odd?
questions.hint: Odd means f(−x) = −f(x).
questions.solution: (−2)³ = −8 = −(2³). So x³ is odd. x² and |x| are even, and √x is neither.

questions.prompt: The graph of f(x) = x² is symmetric about...
questions.hint: Mirror the right half onto the left.
questions.solution: x² is even, and even functions are symmetric about the y-axis.

questions.prompt: Which parent function is neither even nor odd?
questions.hint: It has no values at all for negative x.
questions.solution: √x is not defined for negative x, so f(−x) cannot match f(x) or −f(x). It is neither.

questions.prompt: g(x) = 1/x. Find g(−5).
questions.hint: Put −5 in the bottom of the fraction.

questions.prompt: f is an even function and f(4) = 11. What is f(−4)?
questions.hint: Even means f(−x) = f(x).
questions.solution: Even functions match at opposite inputs, so f(−4) = f(4) = 11.

questions.prompt: f is an odd function and f(5) = −6. What is f(−5)?
questions.hint: Odd means f(−x) = −f(x).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of f(x) = 1/x. How is it symmetric?
choices: About the y-axis, so it is even
About the origin, so it is odd
About the x-axis, so it is even
questions.hint: Rotate the graph 180° around (0, 0).
questions.solution: The two branches match when you rotate the graph half a turn about the origin. That means odd.

questions.prompt: A table shows x = 0, 1, 4, 9 and f(x) = 0, 1, 2, 3. Which parent function is it?
questions.hint: The inputs are perfect squares.

teach.title: Vertical shifts
text: g(x) = f(x) + k moves the graph of f up k units when k is positive and down |k| units when k is negative.
Every point (x, y) on f becomes (x, y + k) on g. Only the y-coordinate changes.

example.problem: The point (2, 7) is on f. Where is it on g(x) = f(x) − 3?

questions.prompt: How does the graph of g(x) = x² + 3 compare with f(x) = x²?
questions.hint: The +3 is added outside, to the whole function.
questions.solution: Adding 3 to the output moves every point up 3.

questions.prompt: How does the graph of g(x) = |x| − 5 compare with f(x) = |x|?
questions.hint: Subtracting from the output moves the graph down.
questions.solution: −5 outside the function moves the graph down 5 units.

questions.prompt: g(x) = x² + 4. The vertex of f(x) = x² is (0, 0). What is the y-coordinate of the vertex of g?
questions.hint: Add 4 to the y-coordinate.
questions.solution: The vertex moves up 4, from (0, 0) to (0, 4). The y-coordinate is 4.

questions.prompt: The point (2, 7) is on the graph of f. If g(x) = f(x) − 3, the point (2, b) is on g. What is b?
questions.hint: Subtract 3 from the y-coordinate.

questions.prompt: The point (−1, 5) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(x) + 2?
questions.hint: A vertical shift changes only one coordinate.
questions.solution: Add 2 to the y-coordinate: (−1, 5 + 2) = (−1, 7).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. It is the graph of f(x) = x² shifted. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: Where is the vertex? Is it above or below the origin?
questions.solution: The vertex is at (0, −4), so the parabola moved down 4. g(x) = x² − 4.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. It is the graph of f(x) = √x shifted. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: Find the starting point of the curve.
questions.solution: The curve starts at (0, 3), so it moved up 3. g(x) = √x + 3.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of g(x) = |x| + 2. What is the y-coordinate of its y-intercept?
questions.hint: The y-intercept is where the graph crosses the y-axis.
questions.solution: The graph crosses the y-axis at (0, 2). The y-coordinate is 2.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x³. Which equation is g(x) = f(x) − 6?
questions.hint: Subtract 6 after cubing.
questions.solution: f(x) − 6 means x³ − 6.

teach.title: Horizontal shifts
text: g(x) = f(x − h) moves the graph right h units. g(x) = f(x + h) moves it left h units. The shift is the opposite of what the sign looks like.
Every point (x, y) on f becomes (x + h, y) on g.

example.problem: The point (4, 1) is on f. Where is it on g(x) = f(x − 3)?

questions.prompt: How does the graph of g(x) = (x − 4)² compare with f(x) = x²?
questions.hint: The 4 is inside, next to x.
questions.solution: x − 4 inside moves the graph right 4 units.

questions.prompt: How does the graph of g(x) = |x + 3| compare with f(x) = |x|?
questions.hint: Inside changes act opposite to the sign.
questions.solution: x + 3 inside moves the graph left 3 units.

questions.prompt: g(x) = (x − 5)². The vertex of f(x) = x² is (0, 0). What is the x-coordinate of the vertex of g?
questions.hint: x − 5 shifts right 5.
questions.solution: The vertex moves right 5, to (5, 0). The x-coordinate is 5.

questions.prompt: g(x) = √(x + 2). The graph of f(x) = √x starts at x = 0. At what x-value does the graph of g start?
questions.hint: The shift is left 2.
questions.solution: x + 2 shifts the graph left 2. It starts at x = −2.

questions.prompt: The point (4, 1) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(x − 3)?
questions.hint: Right or left? Which coordinate changes?
questions.solution: f(x − 3) shifts right 3: add 3 to x. (4 + 3, 1) = (7, 1).

questions.prompt: The point (−2, 6) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(x + 5)?
questions.hint: Plus inside means left.
questions.solution: f(x + 5) shifts left 5: subtract 5 from x. (−2 − 5, 6) = (−7, 6).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. It is the graph of f(x) = |x| shifted. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: Find the corner of the V.
questions.solution: The corner is at (3, 0), so the graph shifted right 3. g(x) = |x − 3|.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of g(x) = (x + 2)². What is the x-coordinate of its vertex?
questions.hint: Read where the lowest point is.
questions.solution: The vertex is at (−2, 0). The x-coordinate is −2.

questions.prompt: f(x − 6) moves the graph of f...
questions.hint: Subtracting inside shifts horizontally in the positive direction.
questions.solution: f(x − 6) is a horizontal shift right 6.

teach.title: Shifting both ways
text: g(x) = f(x − h) + k shifts right h and up k. Read h with the opposite sign, and k with its own sign.
A vertex or key point (a, b) moves to (a + h, b + k).

example.problem: Describe the shift of g(x) = (x − 2)² + 5 from f(x) = x².

questions.prompt: Describe g(x) = (x − 2)² + 5 compared with f(x) = x².
questions.hint: Inside tells left/right (opposite sign). Outside tells up/down.
questions.solution: x − 2 means right 2. +5 means up 5.

questions.prompt: g(x) = (x + 1)² − 6. What is the x-coordinate of its vertex?
questions.hint: Use the opposite of the number inside.
questions.solution: x + 1 shifts left 1, so the vertex x is −1.

questions.prompt: g(x) = |x − 7| + 2. What is the y-coordinate of its vertex?
questions.hint: The number added outside is the y-coordinate.
questions.solution: The vertex is (7, 2). The y-coordinate is 2.

questions.prompt: Find the vertex of g(x) = |x + 4| − 1.
questions.hint: Opposite sign inside, same sign outside.
questions.solution: x + 4 gives x = −4. −1 outside gives y = −1. Vertex (−4, −1).

questions.prompt: The point (3, −2) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(x − 1) + 4?
questions.hint: Add 1 to x for the right shift, then add 4 to y.

questions.prompt: The graph shown is f(x) = x² shifted. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: Read the vertex from the graph.
questions.solution: The vertex is (1, 2). Right 1 gives (x − 1), up 2 gives + 2. g(x) = (x − 1)² + 2.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of g(x) = √(x − 2) + 1. What is g(6)?
questions.hint: Read the y-value above x = 6.

questions.prompt: Describe g(x) = ∛(x + 8) − 3 compared with f(x) = ∛x.
questions.hint: Inside is opposite, outside is the same sign.
questions.solution: x + 8 shifts left 8. −3 shifts down 3.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² and g(x) = f(x − 2) + 3. Find g(5).
questions.hint: Find f(5 − 2) first, then add 3.

teach.title: Writing and analyzing translations
text: To write an equation: subtract h inside, add k outside. Right 2 becomes (x − 2). Down 7 becomes − 7.
A shift moves the domain and range too. If f has domain [0, ∞), then f(x − h) + k has domain [h, ∞), and the range moves up by k.

example.problem: Find the domain and range of g(x) = √(x − 4) + 1.
steps: The parent √x has domain [0, ∞) and range [0, ∞).

questions.prompt: Which is the graph of f(x) = |x| shifted left 2 and down 7?
questions.hint: Left means + inside. Down means − outside.

questions.prompt: Which is f(x) = x² shifted right 6 and up 1?
questions.hint: Right 6 means subtract 6 inside.
questions.solution: Right 6: (x − 6)². Up 1: + 1. So g(x) = (x − 6)² + 1.

questions.hint: Add 3 to 6 first, then take the square root.

questions.prompt: Find the domain and range of g(x) = √(x − 4) + 1.
questions.hint: The parent has domain and range [0, ∞). Shift each.
questions.solution: Right 4 moves the domain to [4, ∞). Up 1 moves the range to [1, ∞).

questions.prompt: Find the range of g(x) = (x + 2)² − 5.
questions.hint: The vertex is the lowest point.
questions.solution: The vertex is (−2, −5) and the parabola opens up. The range is [−5, ∞).

questions.prompt: The point (−3, 4) is on f. It becomes (a, b) on g(x) = f(x − 6) + 1. Find a + b.
questions.hint: Add 6 to x and add 1 to y.

questions.prompt: g(x) = 1/(x − 2) + 3. Which x-value is excluded from its domain?
questions.hint: Set the bottom equal to 0.
questions.solution: x − 2 = 0 gives x = 2.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. It is the graph of f(x) = ∛x shifted. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: The center point of the cube root was (0, 0). Where is it now?
questions.solution: The center moved to (2, 1): right 2, up 1. g(x) = ∛(x − 2) + 1.

questions.prompt: g(x) = 2ˣ + 4. As x → −∞, the graph gets close to the horizontal line y = k. What is k?
questions.hint: 2ˣ gets close to 0 on the left. Then add 4.
questions.solution: As x → −∞, 2ˣ → 0, so g(x) → 4. The line is y = 4.

teach.title: Reflecting over the x-axis
text: g(x) = −f(x) flips the graph over the x-axis. Every y-value changes sign.
A point (x, y) on f becomes (x, −y) on g.

example.problem: The point (3, 5) is on f. Where is it on g(x) = −f(x)?
steps: The negative sign on f(x) flips the y-value.
The x-coordinate stays 3. The y-coordinate becomes −5.

questions.prompt: The graph of g(x) = −f(x) is a reflection of f over...
questions.hint: The negative is outside the function.
questions.solution: A negative outside flips the outputs, which reflects the graph over the x-axis.

questions.prompt: The point (3, 5) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = −f(x)?
questions.hint: Which coordinate changes sign?
questions.solution: Reflecting over the x-axis changes the sign of y only: (3, −5).

questions.prompt: f(2) = −7 and g(x) = −f(x). Find g(2).
questions.hint: Take the opposite of f(2).

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = −f(x). Find g(3).
questions.hint: Find f(3) first, then negate.

questions.prompt: The graph of g(x) = −x² opens...
questions.hint: The parent x² opens up. What does the negative do?
questions.solution: The reflection over the x-axis turns the U upside down, so it opens down.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. It is f(x) = x² − 4 reflected over the x-axis. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: Negate the whole function: −(x² − 4).
questions.solution: −(x² − 4) = −x² + 4. The vertex (0, −4) flips to (0, 4).

questions.prompt: f(x) = x − 3. What is −f(x)?
questions.hint: Distribute the negative to both terms.

questions.prompt: f(x) = √x and g(x) = −f(x). Find g(16).
questions.hint: Find f(16), then negate.

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of g(x) = −√x. What is its range?
questions.hint: The curve goes downward from the origin.
questions.solution: The curve starts at (0, 0) and falls. All y-values are 0 or less. Range: (−∞, 0].

teach.title: Reflecting over the y-axis
text: g(x) = f(−x) flips the graph over the y-axis. The negative is inside, next to x.
A point (x, y) on f becomes (−x, y) on g.

example.problem: The point (6, −2) is on f. Where is it on g(x) = f(−x)?
steps: The negative inside flips the x-value.
The y-coordinate stays −2. The x-coordinate becomes −6.

questions.prompt: The graph of g(x) = f(−x) is a reflection of f over...
questions.hint: The negative is inside, with x.
questions.solution: A negative inside flips the inputs, which reflects the graph over the y-axis.

questions.prompt: The point (3, 5) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(−x)?
questions.hint: Which coordinate changes sign this time?
questions.solution: Reflecting over the y-axis changes the sign of x only: (−3, 5).

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = f(−x). Find g(4).
f(x) = x³ and g(x) = f(−x). Find g(2).
What is the domain of g(x) = √(−x)?
questions.hint: Solve −x ≥ 0. Dividing by a negative flips the inequality.
questions.solution: −x ≥ 0 gives x ≤ 0. Domain: (−∞, 0].

questions.prompt: Look at the graph. It is f(x) = √x reflected over the y-axis. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: The curve goes to the left of the y-axis and stays above the x-axis.
questions.solution: The curve is on the left and goes up. Replace x with −x: g(x) = √(−x).

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² is reflected over the y-axis. What is the new graph?
choices: The graph of y = x² shifted left
The graph of y = x² shifted right
The same graph, because x² is even
questions.hint: Compute (−x)².
questions.solution: (−x)² = x², so f(−x) = f(x). The parabola is symmetric about the y-axis, so it does not change.

questions.prompt: The point (6, −2) is on f. It becomes (a, b) on g(x) = f(−x). Find a + b.
questions.hint: Only x changes sign.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x³ + x. What is f(−x)?
questions.hint: Replace every x with (−x).

teach.title: Which reflection is it?
text: Check where the negative sits. Outside f (−f(x)): x-axis, y changes sign. Inside f (f(−x)): y-axis, x changes sign.
With both, g(x) = −f(−x), the point (x, y) becomes (−x, −y).

example.problem: Reflect the point (2, 5) over both axes.

questions.prompt: g(x) = −|x| is a reflection of f(x) = |x| over...
questions.hint: Is the negative inside or outside?
questions.solution: The negative is outside the absolute value, so it flips the outputs: reflection over the x-axis.

questions.prompt: g(x) = √(−x) is a reflection of f(x) = √x over...
questions.hint: Is the negative inside or outside?
questions.solution: The negative is inside, replacing x, so it reflects over the y-axis.

questions.prompt: For g(x) = −f(−x), the point (a, b) on f goes to...
questions.hint: There are two negatives. One flips x and one flips y.
questions.solution: The inside negative changes x and the outside negative changes y. So (a, b) → (−a, −b).

questions.prompt: The point (2, 5) is on f, and g(x) = −f(−x). Find g(−2).
The point (−4, 3) is reflected over the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of the new point?
questions.hint: Reflecting over the x-axis negates y.
questions.solution: The new point is (−4, −3). Its y-coordinate is −3.

questions.prompt: The point (−4, 3) is reflected over the y-axis. What is the new point?
questions.hint: The y-axis flip changes only x.
questions.solution: The x-coordinate changes sign and y stays: (4, 3).

questions.prompt: Look at the graph of g(x) = −|x| + 3. How is it related to f(x) = |x|?
choices: Reflected over the y-axis, then shifted up 3
Reflected over the x-axis, then shifted up 3
Reflected over the x-axis, then shifted down 3
questions.hint: The V opens down and its corner is above the origin.
questions.solution: The V opens down (reflection over the x-axis) and has its vertex at (0, 3) (up 3).

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² − 9 and g(x) = −f(x). Find the x-values where g(x) = 0. Give both.
questions.hint: g(x) = −x² + 9. Set it equal to 0.
questions.solution: −x² + 9 = 0 gives x² = 9, so x = 3 or x = −3. Reflecting over the x-axis does not move the x-intercepts.

questions.prompt: Which function is unchanged when reflected over the y-axis?
questions.hint: It is the one with f(−x) = f(x).
questions.solution: |−x| = |x|, so |x| is even and its graph looks the same after the reflection. x³ and 1/x are odd and √x is neither.

teach.title: Reflections with shifts
text: Order matters when you read a function. For −f(x) + k, reflect first, then shift. A vertex (h, k) in −a(x − h)² + k means the parabola opens down.
Reflections change domain and range too: −√x has range (−∞, 0], and √(−x) has domain (−∞, 0].

example.problem: Describe g(x) = −|x − 2| + 5.
steps: Negative outside: reflected over the x-axis, so it opens down.
The vertex is (2, 5), the highest point.

questions.prompt: Which is f(x) = x² reflected over the x-axis, then shifted up 3?
questions.hint: Negate first, then add 3.
questions.solution: Reflecting gives −x². Shifting up 3 gives −x² + 3.

questions.prompt: Describe g(x) = −|x − 2| + 5.
questions.hint: The minus sign in front makes the V open down. Read the vertex.
questions.solution: Opening: negative outside, so down. Vertex: x − 2 gives x = 2, + 5 gives y = 5. Vertex (2, 5).

questions.prompt: What is the maximum value of g(x) = −(x + 1)² + 6?
questions.hint: The parabola opens down. Find the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex is (−1, 6). Since it opens down, the maximum value is 6.

questions.prompt: Find the domain and range of g(x) = √(−x) + 2.
questions.hint: The inside negative flips the domain. The + 2 shifts the range up.
questions.solution: −x ≥ 0 gives x ≤ 0, so the domain is (−∞, 0]. The root is at least 0, so the range is [2, ∞).

questions.prompt: f(x) = x³ + 2x and g(x) = f(−x). Find g(1).
Look at the graph. It is f(x) = x² reflected and shifted. Which equation is it?
questions.hint: The parabola opens down, with its vertex at (1, 3).
questions.solution: It opens down, so there is a negative. The vertex (1, 3) means (x − 1)² and + 3.

questions.prompt: The point (2, −3) is on f. It becomes (2, b) on g(x) = −f(x) + 4. Find b.
questions.hint: Negate the y-value, then add 4.

questions.prompt: Find the domain and range of g(x) = −√(x + 5).
questions.hint: x + 5 ≥ 0 for the domain. The negative outside flips the range.
questions.solution: x + 5 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ −5, so the domain is [−5, ∞). The root is at least 0 and the negative flips it, so the range is (−∞, 0].

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of g(x) = −|x| + 4. Give both x-values.
questions.solution: −|x| + 4 = 0 gives |x| = 4, so x = 4 or x = −4.

teach.title: Vertical stretch and compression
text: g(x) = a·f(x) multiplies every y-value by a. The x-values do not change.
If |a| > 1, the graph is stretched vertically (it gets taller and narrower). If 0 < |a| < 1, it is compressed vertically (it gets flatter).

example.problem: A point (2, 3) is on f. Find its image on g(x) = 4f(x).

questions.prompt: How does the graph of g(x) = 3f(x) compare with the graph of f(x)?
choices: Stretched vertically by a factor of 3
Compressed vertically by a factor of 3
Stretched horizontally by a factor of 3
questions.hint: The 3 is outside f, so it acts on the y-values.
questions.solution: Multiplying f(x) by 3 triples every y-value. That is a vertical stretch by a factor of 3.

questions.prompt: f(2) = 5. If g(x) = 4f(x), what is g(2)?
questions.hint: Multiply the output by 4.

questions.prompt: Which function is a vertical stretch of f(x) = x²?
questions.hint: A vertical stretch multiplies the whole function by a number bigger than 1.
questions.solution: 3x² multiplies every y-value by 3, so it is a vertical stretch. 0.3x² is a compression. x² + 3 is a shift up. (x + 3)² is a shift left.

questions.prompt: The point (3, −2) is on f. The point (3, k) is on g(x) = 5f(x). What is k?
questions.hint: Multiply the y-value by 5. Keep the sign.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² + 2 and g(x) = 3f(x). What is the y-intercept of g?
questions.hint: The y-intercept is g(0).

questions.prompt: A table for f has f(1) = 2, f(2) = −3, f(4) = 1.5. If g(x) = 2f(x), what is g(4)?
questions.hint: Find f(4) in the table, then double it.
A fraction between 0 and 1 compresses the graph. Multiply the output by 1/3.

questions.prompt: g(x) = (1/2)f(x). Which statement is true?
choices: Every x-value of f is cut in half; the y-values stay the same.
Every y-value of f is doubled; the x-values stay the same.
Every y-value of f goes down by 1/2.
Every y-value of f is cut in half; the x-values stay the same.
questions.hint: Which coordinate does a number outside f(x) change?
questions.solution: Multiplying the output by 1/2 halves every y-value. The x-values do not change. It is a vertical compression by a factor of 1/2.

teach.title: Vertical compressions and negative a
text: If 0 < |a| < 1, g(x) = a·f(x) is a vertical compression. Each y-value shrinks toward the x-axis.
If a is negative, the graph is also reflected over the x-axis. A stretch or compression never moves the x-intercepts, because 0 times anything is still 0.

example.problem: A point (3, 5) is on f. Find its image on g(x) = −2f(x).
steps: The image point is (3, −10). It is stretched by 2 and flipped over the x-axis.

questions.prompt: g(x) = 0.25f(x). How does g compare with f?
choices: Vertical stretch by a factor of 4
Vertical compression by a factor of 1/4
Horizontal compression by a factor of 1/4
questions.hint: 0.25 is the same as 1/4. It multiplies the outputs.
questions.solution: Multiplying outputs by 1/4 shrinks every y-value toward the x-axis. That is a vertical compression by a factor of 1/4.

questions.prompt: The point (8, 12) is on f. The point (8, k) is on g(x) = (1/4)f(x). What is k?
questions.hint: Multiply the y-value by 1/4.

questions.prompt: The point (2, 4) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = −3f(x)?
questions.hint: Only the y-value changes. Multiply it by −3.
questions.solution: The x-value stays 2. The y-value becomes −3 · 4 = −12. The image is (2, −12).

questions.prompt: How does g(x) = −(1/2)x² compare with f(x) = x²?
choices: Reflected over the y-axis and vertically stretched by 2
Reflected over the x-axis and vertically stretched by 2
Reflected over the x-axis and vertically compressed by 1/2
questions.hint: The negative sign flips it. The 1/2 changes how tall it is.
questions.solution: The negative sign reflects the graph over the x-axis. The factor 1/2 compresses it vertically by 1/2.

questions.prompt: f(5) = −2. If g(x) = −3f(x), what is g(5)?
questions.hint: Multiply −2 by −3.

questions.prompt: Which function makes the parabola y = x² narrower?
questions.hint: Narrower means the y-values grow faster. You need a multiplier bigger than 1 in size.
questions.solution: 5x² makes every y-value 5 times larger, so the parabola gets narrower. 0.2x², x²/2, and −x²/5 all make it wider.

questions.prompt: The point (4, 6) is on f and the point (4, −9) is on g(x) = a·f(x). What is a?
questions.hint: Solve a · 6 = −9.

questions.prompt: f has zeros at x = −1 and x = 3. g(x) = 2f(x). What are the zeros of g?
questions.hint: Where does 2 · f(x) = 0?
questions.solution: 2f(x) = 0 exactly when f(x) = 0. A vertical stretch does not move the zeros. They stay at x = −1 and x = 3.

teach.title: Horizontal stretch and compression
text: g(x) = f(bx) changes the x-values. Each x-value is divided by b. The y-values stay the same.
If |b| > 1 the graph is compressed horizontally by a factor of 1/|b|. If 0 < |b| < 1 it is stretched horizontally by a factor of 1/|b|. This is the opposite of what you might guess.

example.problem: A point (8, −1) is on f. Find its image on g(x) = f(4x).
steps: The image point is (2, −1). The graph is squeezed toward the y-axis.

questions.prompt: How does g(x) = f(2x) compare with f(x)?
choices: Stretched horizontally by a factor of 2
Stretched vertically by a factor of 2
Compressed horizontally by a factor of 1/2
Compressed vertically by a factor of 1/2
questions.hint: The 2 is inside f, so it acts on the x-values.
questions.solution: Inside, 2x reaches each output in half the x-distance. So x-values are halved: a horizontal compression by a factor of 1/2.

questions.prompt: The point (6, 5) is on f. The point (k, 5) is on g(x) = f(2x). What is k?
questions.hint: Divide the x-value by 2.

questions.prompt: How does g(x) = f(x/3) compare with f(x)?
choices: Compressed horizontally by a factor of 3
Stretched horizontally by a factor of 3
Stretched vertically by a factor of 3
Compressed vertically by a factor of 1/3
questions.hint: x/3 is the same as (1/3)x, so b = 1/3.
questions.solution: b = 1/3, and each x-value is divided by 1/3, which means multiplied by 3. That is a horizontal stretch by a factor of 3.

questions.prompt: The point (4, −1) is on f. The point (k, −1) is on g(x) = f(x/2). What is k?
questions.hint: b = 1/2. Divide the x-value by 1/2.
questions.solution: Dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2. k = 4 · 2 = 8.

questions.prompt: The point (−6, 9) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(3x)?
questions.hint: Only the x-value changes. Divide it by 3.
questions.solution: x becomes −6 ÷ 3 = −2. The y-value stays 9. The image is (−2, 9).

questions.prompt: f has a zero at x = 12. g(x) = f(4x). Where is the zero of g?
questions.hint: Solve 4x = 12.
questions.solution: g(x) = 0 when 4x = 12, so x = 3.

questions.prompt: Which function is a horizontal compression of f by a factor of 1/5?
questions.hint: A compression by 1/5 means each x-value is divided by 5.
questions.solution: To divide x-values by 5, use b = 5: g(x) = f(5x). f(x/5) is a stretch, and 5f(x) and f(x)/5 change y-values.

questions.prompt: The point (9, 2) on f is mapped to (3, 2) on g(x) = f(bx). What is b?
questions.hint: The new x-value is 9 ÷ b.

teach.title: Both together
text: For g(x) = a·f(bx), a point (x, y) on f goes to (x/b, a·y). Do the x-value and the y-value separately.
For some functions the two effects look alike. For f(x) = x², f(3x) = 9x², which is also a vertical stretch by 9.

example.problem: The point (9, 2) is on f. Find its image on g(x) = −3f(x/3).

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² and g(x) = f(3x). Which is g(x) simplified?
questions.hint: Replace x with 3x inside x².
questions.solution: g(x) = (3x)² = 9x².

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² − 9 has zeros at x = 3 and x = −3. Find the zeros of g(x) = f(x/2).
questions.hint: Solve (x/2)² − 9 = 0, or double each zero.
questions.solution: g(x) = (x/2)² − 9 = 0 gives x/2 = ±3, so x = ±6. The graph is stretched horizontally by 2, so each zero doubles.

questions.prompt: The point (4, −6) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = −2f(x/2)?
questions.hint: x/2 divides by b = 1/2, so x doubles. The −2 acts on y.

questions.prompt: f(x) = √x and g(x) = 2f(x). What is g(9)?
questions.hint: Find f(9) first.

questions.prompt: Which describes h(x) = (1/3)f(2x)?
choices: Horizontal compression by 1/2 and vertical compression by 1/3
Horizontal stretch by 2 and vertical stretch by 3
Horizontal stretch by 2 and vertical compression by 1/3
Horizontal compression by 1/3 and vertical compression by 1/2
questions.hint: The 2 is inside f. The 1/3 is outside f.
questions.solution: Inside: 2x compresses x-values by 1/2. Outside: 1/3 compresses y-values by 1/3.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = f(3x). What is g(2)?
The point (6, −3) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = 4f(x/3)?
questions.hint: x/3 means b = 1/3. Divide x by 1/3, then multiply y by 4.

questions.prompt: The point (10, 6) on f is mapped to (5, 18) on g(x) = a·f(bx). What is a · b?
questions.hint: Find b from the x-values and a from the y-values.
questions.solution: x: 10 ÷ b = 5, so b = 2. y: a · 6 = 18, so a = 3. Then a · b = 6.

teach.title: Reading g(x) = a·f(x − h) + k
text: Each number does one job. h shifts the graph right (if h is positive). a stretches, compresses, or flips it vertically. k shifts it up.
x − h with a minus sign moves right. x + 3 is x − (−3), so it moves left 3.

example.problem: Describe g(x) = 2f(x − 3) + 1.
steps: 2 outside: vertical stretch by a factor of 2.

questions.prompt: Which describes g(x) = 2f(x − 3) + 1?
questions.hint: Inside the parentheses, x − 3 moves the graph right.
questions.solution: x − 3 shifts right 3. The 2 multiplies the outputs: vertical stretch by 2. The + 1 shifts up 1.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² and g(x) = 2f(x − 3) + 1. What is g(5)?
questions.hint: Work from the inside out: x − 3 first, then f, then 2 times, then + 1.

questions.prompt: Which describes g(x) = −f(x + 4) − 2?
choices: Reflect over the y-axis, left 4, down 2
Reflect over the x-axis, left 4, down 2
Reflect over the x-axis, right 4, down 2
Reflect over the x-axis, left 4, up 2
questions.hint: x + 4 is x − (−4). The minus in front of f flips the outputs.
questions.solution: −f flips over the x-axis. x + 4 shifts left 4. − 2 shifts down 2.

questions.prompt: The point (1, 3) is on f. The point (k, 5) is on g(x) = f(x − 4) + 2. What is k?
questions.hint: The shift right adds 4 to the x-value.
questions.solution: x: 1 + 4 = 5. y: 3 + 2 = 5, which matches. So k = 5.

questions.prompt: The point (1, 3) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(x − 4) + 2?
questions.hint: Add 4 to x for the right shift. Add 2 to y for the up shift.

questions.prompt: The point (−2, 4) is on f. The point (−3, k) is on g(x) = 3f(x + 1) − 5. What is k?
questions.hint: Multiply the y-value by 3 first, then subtract 5.

questions.prompt: Which function shifts f left 2 units and down 5 units?
questions.hint: Left is + inside. Down is − outside.
questions.solution: Left 2 is f(x + 2). Down 5 is − 5 after f. So g(x) = f(x + 2) − 5.

questions.prompt: f(x) = √x and g(x) = 2f(x − 1) + 3. What is g(5)?
questions.hint: x − 1 first: 5 − 1 = 4.

teach.title: Step by step with a key point
text: To map a key point (x, y) on f to g(x) = a·f(x − h) + k, use (x + h, a·y + k).
Stretch first, then shift. 3f(x) + 2 means multiply by 3, then add 2. It does not mean add 2, then multiply.

example.problem: The point (5, −2) is on f. Find its image on g(x) = −2f(x − 1) + 3.

questions.prompt: The parent function is f(x) = |x| with vertex (0, 0). Where is the vertex of g(x) = −2f(x − 3) + 5?
questions.hint: Shift (0, 0) right 3, then up 5. The −2 does nothing to 0.

questions.prompt: The point (2, −1) is on f. The point (0, k) is on g(x) = −3f(x + 2) + 4. What is k?
questions.hint: Multiply by −3 first, then add 4.

questions.prompt: The point (2, −1) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = −3f(x + 2) + 4?
questions.hint: Left 2 changes x from 2 to 0.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x³ and (2, 8) is on f. The point (3, k) is on g(x) = (1/2)f(x − 1) − 3. What is k?
questions.hint: Take half of 8, then subtract 3.

questions.prompt: The point (1, 5) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = 3f(x) + 2?
questions.hint: Stretch first, then shift: 3 · 5, then + 2.
questions.solution: y: 3 · 5 + 2 = 15 + 2 = 17. The x-value stays 1. The image is (1, 17). (1, 21) comes from adding 2 before multiplying, which is the wrong order.

questions.prompt: f(4) = −2 and g(x) = −2f(x − 1) + 6. What is g(5)?
(−3, 0) is an x-intercept of f. Where is the image of that point on g(x) = 2f(x − 4)?
questions.hint: There is no + k, so the y-value 0 stays 0.

questions.prompt: f(x) = |x| and g(x) = −2f(x − 1) + 8. What is g(−3)?

teach.title: Domain and range after a combined move
text: Move the endpoints of the domain and range with the same rules. The domain changes only by the shift h (right adds h). The range changes by a and k: multiply, then add k.
If a is negative, the endpoints swap order. Write the smaller number first.

example.problem: f has domain [0, 8] and range [1, 5]. Find the domain and range of g(x) = 3f(x + 2) − 4.
steps: Domain: x + 2 shifts left 2, so subtract 2 from each end: [−2, 6].

questions.prompt: f has domain [−2, 6]. What is the domain of g(x) = f(x − 3) + 1?
questions.hint: Only the shift inside changes the domain.
questions.solution: Right 3 adds 3 to each end: [−2 + 3, 6 + 3] = [1, 9]. The + 1 does not affect the domain.

questions.prompt: f has range [−1, 4]. What is the range of g(x) = f(x − 3) + 1?
questions.hint: Only the shift outside changes the range.
questions.solution: Up 1 adds 1 to each end: [−1 + 1, 4 + 1] = [0, 5].

questions.prompt: f has range [−1, 4]. What is the range of g(x) = −2f(x) + 1?
questions.hint: Multiply by −2 first. The ends swap order. Then add 1.
questions.solution: −2 · (−1) = 2 and −2 · 4 = −8, so after multiplying the range is [−8, 2]. Adding 1 gives [−7, 3].

questions.prompt: f has a minimum value of −3. What is the minimum value of g(x) = 2f(x + 1) + 4?
questions.hint: Stretch by 2 first, then shift up 4. The shift inside does not change values.
questions.solution: 2 · (−3) = −6, then −6 + 4 = −2. The minimum value of g is −2.

questions.prompt: f has a maximum value of 5. What is the maximum value of g(x) = 0.5f(x − 4) − 1?
questions.hint: Half of 5, then subtract 1.

questions.prompt: f has a maximum of 5 at x = 2. What does g(x) = −f(x − 1) + 3 have?
questions.hint: The negative sign turns a maximum into a minimum.
questions.solution: The reflection turns the maximum into a minimum. Value: −5 + 3 = −2. Location: 2 + 1 = 3.

questions.prompt: f(x) = √x starts at x = 0. g(x) = −3f(x − 5) + 2. At what x-value does g start?
questions.hint: The domain of g starts where x − 5 = 0.
questions.solution: x − 5 ≥ 0 means x ≥ 5. The graph of g starts at x = 5.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x². What is the range of g(x) = −f(x + 3) + 4?
questions.hint: The vertex is the highest point because the graph opens down.
questions.solution: The vertex is at (−3, 4) and the parabola opens down, so every y-value is at most 4. The range is y ≤ 4.

teach.title: Adding a horizontal stretch
text: A function can also include f(b(x − h)). A point (x, y) goes to (x/b + h, a·y + k) for g(x) = a·f(b(x − h)) + k.
First divide x by b, then add h. For y, multiply by a, then add k.

example.problem: The point (4, −5) is on f. Find its image on g(x) = 2f(½(x + 1)).
steps: Here b = ½, h = −1, a = 2, k = 0.

questions.prompt: The point (4, 1) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(2(x − 3))?
questions.hint: Divide x by 2, then add 3.
questions.solution: x: 4 ÷ 2 = 2, then 2 + 3 = 5. The y-value stays 1. The image is (5, 1).

questions.prompt: The point (6, −4) is on f. The point (k, −12) is on g(x) = 3f(½(x − 1)). What is k?
questions.hint: Divide by ½, which is the same as multiplying by 2. Then add 1.

questions.prompt: Which equation is f stretched vertically by 2, compressed horizontally by 1/2, moved right 1 and up 3?
questions.hint: Compressing by 1/2 horizontally means b = 2.
questions.solution: Vertical stretch by 2 gives a = 2. Horizontal compression by 1/2 gives b = 2. Right 1 is (x − 1). Up 3 is + 3.

questions.prompt: The point (−4, 2) is on f. What is the x-coordinate of its image on g(x) = −f(2(x + 1)) + 5?
questions.hint: Divide by 2 first, then shift left 1.

questions.prompt: The point (6, −1) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = −f(2(x + 1)) + 5?
questions.hint: x: divide by 2, then subtract 1. y: negate, then add 5.

questions.prompt: f(6) = 4 and g(x) = 2f(3x) − 1. What is g(2)?
questions.hint: 3x = 6 when x = 2.

questions.prompt: The point (4, 3) is on f. What is the x-coordinate of its image on g(x) = −2f(2(x − 1)) + 4?
questions.hint: Divide 4 by 2, then add 1.

questions.prompt: A student maps (4, 3) to (9, 3) for g(x) = f(2(x − 1)). What was the mistake?
choices: Multiplied x by 2 instead of dividing by 2
Divided x by 2 and forgot the shift
questions.hint: Check what f(2x) does to x-values.
questions.solution: The correct x is 4 ÷ 2 + 1 = 3. The student did 4 · 2 + 1 = 9. Inside f, a multiplier b divides the x-value.

teach.title: From words to an equation
text: Start with the parent function. Right h means x − h. Left h means x + h. Up k means + k. Down k means − k. A flip over the x-axis puts a minus in front of the function.
Order: do the stretch or flip, then the shift. Example for f(x) = x²: a(x − h)² + k.

example.problem: Write the equation for y = x² moved left 5 and down 2.
steps: Left 5 means replace x with x + 5: (x + 5)².

questions.prompt: Which is y = x² shifted right 4 and up 3?
questions.hint: Right goes with a minus inside the parentheses.
questions.solution: Right 4: (x − 4)². Up 3: + 3. So y = (x − 4)² + 3.

questions.prompt: Which is y = |x| shifted left 2 and down 5?
questions.hint: Left means + inside. Down means − outside.

questions.prompt: The graph of y = √x is shifted right 6, so the new equation is y = √(x − h). What is h?
questions.hint: Right 6 means x − 6.

questions.prompt: Which is y = x³ reflected over the x-axis and then shifted up 1?
questions.hint: The reflection over the x-axis puts a minus on the whole function.
questions.solution: Reflect: −x³. Shift up 1: −x³ + 1.

questions.prompt: y = |x| is stretched vertically by 3 and then moved down 4. In y = a|x| + k, what is k?
questions.hint: Down 4 is a negative k.
questions.solution: The equation is y = 3|x| − 4, so a = 3 and k = −4.

questions.prompt: Which is y = x² compressed vertically by 1/2 and shifted left 3?
questions.hint: A vertical compression by 1/2 multiplies by 1/2.
questions.solution: Left 3: (x + 3)². Compression by 1/2: ½(x + 3)². So y = ½(x + 3)².

questions.prompt: y = −2(x + 1)² + 7 has its vertex at (h, k). What is h?
questions.solution: The vertex is (−1, 7), so h = −1.

questions.prompt: Which is y = √x shifted left 5 and up 2?
questions.hint: The shift left goes inside the root.

teach.title: Reading an equation off a graph
text: Find the key point, the vertex or the start point, to get h and k. Then use one other point to find a.
For y = a(x − h)² + k, plug in the other point and solve for a. If the graph opens down, a is negative.

example.problem: A parabola has vertex (−2, 5), opens down, and passes through (0, 1). Find its equation.
steps: Plug in (0, 1): 1 = a(2)² + 5, so 4a = −4 and a = −1.

questions.prompt: The graph shows a transformation of f(x) = x². Which is its equation?
questions.hint: Read the vertex off the graph. Then use it as (h, k).
questions.solution: The vertex is (3, 1), so h = 3 and k = 1. The equation is y = (x − 3)² + 1.

questions.prompt: Which equation matches this V-shaped graph, a transformation of f(x) = |x|?
questions.hint: The vertex is at (−2, −3).
questions.solution: The vertex (−2, −3) gives h = −2 and k = −3. The graph opens up, so a = 1. The equation is y = |x + 2| − 3.

questions.prompt: The graph shows a transformation of f(x) = √x. Which is its equation?
questions.hint: The graph starts at (1, 2).
questions.solution: The start point (1, 2) gives h = 1 and k = 2. The equation is y = √(x − 1) + 2.

questions.prompt: The graph shows a transformation of f(x) = x³. Which is its equation?
questions.hint: The center of the cubic, where it flattens, is at (2, −1).
questions.solution: The center point (2, −1) gives h = 2 and k = −1. The equation is y = (x − 2)³ − 1.

questions.prompt: This graph is a transformation of f(x) = |x| that opens downward. Which is its equation?
questions.hint: It opens down, so there is a minus sign in front.
questions.solution: The vertex (1, 3) gives h = 1 and k = 3. It opens down, so a is negative: y = −|x − 1| + 3.

questions.prompt: Which equation matches this parabola, a transformation of f(x) = x²?
questions.hint: The vertex is (−1, −3). Then check another point, like (0, −1).
questions.solution: Vertex (−1, −3) gives y = a(x + 1)² − 3. The point (0, −1): a(1) − 3 = −1, so a = 2. The equation is y = 2(x + 1)² − 3.

questions.prompt: The graph is y = a(x − 1)² + 2. It passes through (3, −2). What is a?
questions.hint: Plug in x = 3 and y = −2, then solve for a.

questions.prompt: The graph is y = a|x + 2| + 1. It passes through (0, 5). What is a?
questions.hint: Plug in x = 0 and y = 5.

teach.title: Several transformations at once
text: Build the equation in order: parent function, then reflection and stretch (a), then the shifts (h and k).
If you are given a vertex and one more point, find h and k from the vertex. Then substitute the point and solve for a.

example.problem: Write the equation for f(x) = √x reflected over the x-axis, stretched by 2, moved left 1 and down 3.

questions.prompt: Which is y = |x| reflected over the x-axis, stretched by 3, moved right 2 and up 4?
questions.hint: a is −3. Right 2 puts − 2 inside.
questions.solution: Reflect and stretch: a = −3. Right 2: |x − 2|. Up 4: + 4. y = −3|x − 2| + 4.

questions.prompt: Which is y = √x compressed vertically by 1/2, moved left 4 and down 1?
questions.hint: Left 4 is + 4 inside the root.
questions.solution: Compression: a = ½. Left 4: √(x + 4). Down 1: − 1.

questions.prompt: A parabola y = a(x − 2)² − 5 has vertex (2, −5) and passes through (4, 3). What is a?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 4 and y = 3.

questions.prompt: Which is y = x³ reflected over the x-axis, moved right 1 and down 3?
questions.hint: Put the minus on the whole cube. Then shift.
questions.solution: Reflect: −(…)³. Right 1: (x − 1). Down 3: − 3. y = −(x − 1)³ − 3.

questions.prompt: y = a|x − 3| + 1 has vertex (3, 1) and passes through (5, −3). What is a?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 5 and y = −3.

questions.prompt: A table for g has the points (−1, 5), (0, 2), (1, 5), (2, 14). Which equation fits?
questions.hint: g(0) = 2 gives the vertical shift. Then check g(1).
questions.solution: g(0) = 2 gives k = 2 and the vertex is (0, 2). g(1) = 5 gives a + 2 = 5, so a = 3. Check g(2) = 12 + 2 = 14. ✓

questions.prompt: g(x) = a√x + k passes through (0, 3) and (4, 7). What is a?
questions.hint: g(0) gives k. Then use the second point.
questions.solution: g(0) = 3 gives k = 3. Then g(4) = a · 2 + 3 = 7, so 2a = 4 and a = 2.

questions.prompt: Which is y = 1/x shifted right 3 and up 2?
questions.hint: The shift right goes inside the denominator.

teach.title: Writing with a point and a description
text: Use the vertex (h, k) to write y = a(x − h)² + k, or y = a|x − h| + k. Use any extra point to find a.
Check your equation by plugging in a second point. If the answer does not match, recheck the signs of h and k.

example.problem: Find the equation of a parabola with vertex (2, −1) that passes through (4, 7).

questions.prompt: A parabola y = a(x + 3)² + 4 passes through (−1, −4). What is a?
questions.hint: Substitute x = −1 and y = −4.

questions.prompt: Which equation matches this graph, which has a vertex and straight sides like f(x) = |x|?
questions.hint: Vertex first. Then check (4, 2): how far down does it go in 2 steps?
questions.solution: The vertex is (2, 3), and the graph opens down. One step 2 right goes down 1, so the slope is −½. y = −½|x − 2| + 3.

questions.prompt: The graph shows a transformation of f(x) = ∛x. Which is its equation?
questions.hint: The center is (−3, −1). One step right, to x = −2, gives y = 1.
questions.solution: The center (−3, −1) gives h = −3 and k = −1. At x = −2, y = 1: a · ∛1 − 1 = 1, so a = 2. y = 2∛(x + 3) − 1.

questions.prompt: y = a|x − 4| − 2 has vertex (4, −2) and passes through (0, 6). What is a?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 0 and y = 6.

questions.prompt: Which sequence of steps turns y = x² into y = −½(x + 4)² + 1?
choices: Stretch by 2 and flip over the x-axis, move left 4, move up 1
Compress by ½ and flip over the x-axis, move left 4, move up 1
Compress by ½ and flip over the x-axis, move right 4, move up 1
Compress by ½ and flip over the y-axis, move left 4, move down 1
questions.hint: Read a, then h, then k.
questions.solution: a = −½ compresses by ½ and flips over the x-axis. (x + 4) moves left 4. + 1 moves up 1.

questions.prompt: y = a/(x − 2) + 1 passes through (3, 4). What is a?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 3 and y = 4.

questions.prompt: A parabola has vertex (1, −2) and y-intercept −5. Which is its equation?
questions.hint: The y-intercept is the point (0, −5).

questions.prompt: g(x) = a√(x + 1) + k passes through (0, 5) and (3, 8). What is k?
questions.hint: Two equations: a + k = 5 and 2a + k = 8.
questions.solution: g(0) = a · 1 + k = 5 and g(3) = a · 2 + k = 8. Subtract: a = 3. Then k = 5 − 3 = 2.

teach.title: Vertex and direction
text: y = a|x − h| + k is a V shape. The vertex is the point (h, k). The axis of symmetry is the line x = h.
If a > 0 the V opens up and k is the minimum value. If a < 0 it opens down and k is the maximum value.

example.problem: Find the vertex of y = |x + 6| − 1 and tell whether it opens up or down.
steps: a = 1 is positive, so it opens up.

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of y = |x − 4| + 2?
questions.hint: The vertex is (h, k) in y = a|x − h| + k.
questions.solution: x − 4 gives h = 4. + 2 gives k = 2. The vertex is (4, 2).

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of y = |x + 3| − 5?
questions.solution: h = −3 and k = −5. The vertex is (−3, −5).

questions.prompt: Does y = −2|x − 1| + 6 open up or down?
choices: Down, because the vertex is at x = 1
questions.hint: Look at the number multiplying the absolute value.
questions.solution: The sign of a decides the direction. a = −2 is negative, so it opens down.

questions.prompt: What is the x-coordinate of the vertex of y = 3|x + 7| − 1?
questions.solution: h = −7. The vertex is (−7, −1), so the x-coordinate is −7.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum value of y = 2|x − 5| + 3?
questions.hint: The absolute value part is never negative. When is it 0?
questions.solution: |x − 5| ≥ 0, so y ≥ 3. The minimum value is 3, at x = 5.

questions.prompt: The graph shows y = |x − 2| + 1. What is its vertex?
questions.hint: Find the lowest point of the V.
questions.solution: The lowest point of the V is at x = 2, y = 1. The vertex is (2, 1).

questions.prompt: The axis of symmetry of y = |x + 6| − 2 is the line x = ?
questions.hint: The axis passes through the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex is (−6, −2), so the axis of symmetry is x = −6.

questions.prompt: What is true about y = −|x| + 4?
choices: It has a minimum value of 4 at x = 0
It has a maximum value of 4 at x = 4
It has a maximum value of 4 at x = 0
It has a minimum value of −4 at x = 0
questions.hint: It opens down. The vertex is the top.
questions.solution: a = −1, so it opens down. The vertex is (0, 4), the highest point. So the maximum is 4 at x = 0.

teach.title: Slope of each side
text: The two sides of the V are straight lines. For y = a|x − h| + k, the right side has slope a and the left side has slope −a.
A larger |a| makes the V narrower. A smaller |a| makes it wider.

example.problem: Find the slope of each side of y = −½|x + 2| + 1.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the right side of y = 3|x − 1| + 2?
questions.hint: The right side has slope a.
questions.solution: a = 3, so the right side has slope 3.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the left side of y = 3|x − 1| + 2?
questions.hint: The left side has slope −a.
questions.solution: The left side has slope −a = −3.

questions.prompt: What are the slopes of the sides of y = −½|x + 2| + 1?
choices: Right side −½ and left side ½
Right side ½ and left side −½
questions.hint: Right side: a. Left side: −a.
questions.solution: a = −½. The right side has slope −½ and the left side has slope ½.

questions.prompt: What is y when x = 5 for y = 2|x − 3| − 4?
questions.hint: Work inside the absolute value first.

questions.prompt: The graph shows y = 2|x − 1| − 3. What are the slopes of the two sides?
questions.hint: From the vertex (1, −3), go 1 right. How far does y rise?
questions.solution: From the vertex (1, −3), one step right goes to (2, −1), a rise of 2. The right slope is 2 and the left slope is −2.

questions.prompt: The left side of y = a|x − 2| + 1 has slope −5. What is a?
questions.hint: The left side has slope −a.

questions.prompt: Which graph is the narrowest?
questions.hint: The steeper the sides, the narrower the V.
questions.solution: The sides of y = 4|x| have slope ±4, steeper than the others, so it is the narrowest.

questions.prompt: What is y when x = −5 for y = −3|x + 2| + 10?
questions.hint: x + 2 = −3 inside the bars.

teach.title: Intercepts
text: The y-intercept is the value of y when x = 0. Plug in 0 and simplify.

For x-intercepts, set y = 0. Isolate the absolute value, then split into two cases: the inside equals the positive number, or the inside equals the negative number. If the absolute value would equal a negative number, there are no x-intercepts.

example.problem: Find the x-intercepts of y = 3|x − 2| − 9.
steps: x − 2 = 3 gives x = 5. x − 2 = −3 gives x = −1.
The x-intercepts are x = 5 and x = −1.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = |x − 3| + 1?
questions.hint: Let x = 0.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = 2|x + 4| − 5?
questions.hint: Let x = 0.

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = |x − 2| − 5.
questions.hint: Set y = 0 and write |x − 2| = 5. Two cases.
questions.solution: |x − 2| = 5 gives x − 2 = 5 or x − 2 = −5. So x = 7 or x = −3.

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = 2|x + 1| − 8.
questions.hint: Get |x + 1| alone first.

questions.prompt: How many x-intercepts does y = −|x − 1| − 2 have?
questions.hint: It opens down. Where is its vertex?
questions.solution: The vertex is (1, −2) and the V opens down, so the graph stays below the x-axis. There are no x-intercepts.

questions.prompt: Which function has two x-intercepts?
questions.hint: A V that opens up needs its vertex below the x-axis.
questions.solution: y = |x + 2| − 3 opens up with vertex (−2, −3), below the x-axis, so it crosses the axis twice. The others never reach y = 0.

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = −2|x − 3| + 8.
questions.hint: Set y = 0 and divide by −2.

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = ½|x + 6| − 2.
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 2 after moving the 2.
questions.solution: ½|x + 6| = 2, so |x + 6| = 4. Then x + 6 = 4 gives x = −2, and x + 6 = −4 gives x = −10.

teach.title: Writing and using absolute value equations
text: To write an equation, use the vertex for h and k. Then use any other point to find a.
To solve a real situation, plug in the value you know, then check whether you need the positive or negative case.

example.problem: A V has vertex (2, 1) and passes through (4, 7). Find y = a|x − 2| + 1.

questions.prompt: A V opens up with vertex (3, −2) and sides with slope ±2. Which is its equation?
questions.solution: Vertex (3, −2) gives h = 3 and k = −2. The slope is 2 on the right, so a = 2.

questions.prompt: y = a|x + 1| + 4 has vertex (−1, 4) and passes through (2, −5). What is a?
questions.hint: Plug in x = 2 and y = −5.

questions.prompt: The graph shows a V. Which is its equation?
questions.hint: The vertex is at (−3, 2) and the V opens down.
questions.solution: The vertex (−3, 2) gives h = −3 and k = 2. It opens down with slopes ±1, so a = −1. y = −|x + 3| + 2.

questions.prompt: y = a|x − 4| + 1 passes through (0, 13). What is a?
questions.hint: Plug in x = 0 and y = 13.

questions.prompt: A valley has height h = ½|x − 20| + 3, with x in meters. What is the height at x = 0?
questions.hint: Work inside the bars first.

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = −3|x − 2| + 12.
questions.hint: Isolate the absolute value first.

questions.prompt: Which statement about y = −2|x + 5| + 4 is true?
choices: The vertex is (−5, 4) and the maximum value is 4
The vertex is (5, 4) and the maximum value is 4
The vertex is (−5, 4) and the minimum value is 4
The vertex is (−5, −4) and the maximum value is −4
questions.hint: Read h and k. Then use the sign of a.
