questions.solution: x + 5 gives h = −5. k = 4. The vertex is (−5, 4). a = −2 is negative, so it opens down and the maximum is 4.

questions.prompt: For what x-values does 2|x − 1| − 3 equal 5? Give both.
questions.hint: Solve 2|x − 1| − 3 = 5. First isolate |x − 1|.

teach.title: Which piece do I use?
text: A piecewise function uses a different rule on different parts of the domain. Look at the condition next to each rule. Use the rule whose condition is true for your x-value.
Check the condition first. Then put the x-value into that rule only.

example.problem: f(x) = x + 2 if x < 1, and f(x) = 3x − 4 if x ≥ 1. Find f(5).

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 if x < 0, and x² − 3 if x ≥ 0. Which rule do you use to find f(4)?
questions.hint: Check which condition 4 satisfies.
questions.solution: 4 ≥ 0 is true, so use x² − 3.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 if x < 0, and x² − 3 if x ≥ 0. Find f(4).
questions.hint: Use the rule for x ≥ 0.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 if x < 0, and x² − 3 if x ≥ 0. Find f(−2).
questions.hint: −2 < 0, so use the first rule.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 if x < 0, and x² − 3 if x ≥ 0. Find f(0).
questions.solution: 0 < 0 is false, but 0 ≥ 0 is true. Use x² − 3: f(0) = 0 − 3 = −3.

questions.prompt: g(x) = x + 5 if x ≤ −1, and 2x if x > −1. Which rule do you use to find g(−1)?
questions.hint: Which condition includes the equals sign?
questions.solution: x ≤ −1 includes −1, so use x + 5. The other rule needs x > −1, which excludes −1.

questions.prompt: g(x) = x + 5 if x ≤ −1, and 2x if x > −1. Find g(−1).
questions.hint: Use x + 5.

questions.prompt: g(x) = x + 5 if x ≤ −1, and 2x if x > −1. Find g(3).
g(x) = x + 5 if x ≤ −1, and 2x if x > −1. Find g(−6).

teach.title: Three pieces and the boundary
text: Some functions have three or more pieces. Compare your x-value with each boundary in order. At a boundary, only the rule with ≤ or ≥ includes it.
The domain is every x-value covered by at least one piece. If the pieces together cover everything, the domain is all real numbers. If a boundary value is left out of every piece, exclude it.

example.problem: h(x) = −x if x < −2; 4 if −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; 2x − 2 if x > 3. Find h(−5).

questions.prompt: h(x) = −x if x < −2; 4 if −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; 2x − 2 if x > 3. Find h(−7).
h(x) = −x if x < −2; 4 if −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; 2x − 2 if x > 3. Find h(1).
questions.hint: Which interval holds 1?

questions.prompt: h(x) = −x if x < −2; 4 if −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; 2x − 2 if x > 3. Find h(3).
questions.hint: The middle rule includes 3.
questions.solution: 3 is in the middle interval (it has ≤ 3). So h(3) = 4. The third rule would need x > 3.

questions.prompt: h(x) = −x if x < −2; 4 if −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; 2x − 2 if x > 3. Find h(5).
h(x) = −x if x < −2; 4 if −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; 2x − 2 if x > 3. What happens to the graph at x = −2?
choices: It has a closed dot at (−2, 2) and an open dot at (−2, 4)
It has a closed dot at (−2, 4) and an open dot at (−2, 2)
It has closed dots at both (−2, 2) and (−2, 4)
It has an open dot at (−2, 4) and no other dot
questions.hint: The first rule has x < −2, so −2 is excluded from it. The second rule includes −2.
questions.solution: The first rule gives −(−2) = 2 at the edge, but x < −2 excludes it: open dot at (−2, 2). The middle rule includes −2: closed dot at (−2, 4).

questions.prompt: What is the domain of h(x) = −x if x < −2; 4 if −2 ≤ x ≤ 3; 2x − 2 if x > 3?
questions.hint: Do the three conditions leave any gaps?
questions.solution: x < −2, then −2 ≤ x ≤ 3, then x > 3 covers every number, so the domain is all real numbers.

questions.prompt: k(x) = x + 1 if x < 0; x − 1 if x > 0. What is the domain of k?
questions.hint: Which x-value is in neither condition?
questions.solution: x = 0 is not less than 0 and not greater than 0, so no rule covers it. The domain is all real numbers except 0.

questions.prompt: k(x) = x + 1 if x < 0; x − 1 if x > 0. Find k(−3) + k(3).
questions.hint: Find each value separately.

teach.title: Reading a piecewise graph
text: A closed dot means the point is on the graph. An open dot means the point is not on the graph, but the graph gets close to it.
Where two pieces meet at the same x-value, a closed dot on one and an open dot on the other tells you which y-value counts there. If both pieces end at the same point, the graph is connected.

example.problem: The left piece ends at an open dot at (2, 1). The right piece starts with a closed dot at (2, 4). Find f(2).
steps: The open dot at (2, 1) is not on the graph.
The closed dot at (2, 4) is on the graph.

questions.prompt: A graph has a closed dot at (2, 5) and an open dot at (2, 1). What is f(2)?
questions.hint: Which dot is on the graph?
questions.solution: The closed dot is on the graph, so f(2) = 5. The open dot is not part of the graph.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² if x ≤ 1; 3 − x if x > 1. What happens at x = 1?
choices: Closed dot at (1, 1) and open dot at (1, 2)
Open dot at (1, 1) and closed dot at (1, 2)
questions.hint: Plug x = 1 into each rule. Then see which condition includes 1.
questions.solution: x² gives 1 at x = 1 and its condition is x ≤ 1, so closed dot at (1, 1). 3 − x gives 2 at x = 1 and its condition is x > 1, so open dot at (1, 2).

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² if x ≤ 1; 3 − x if x > 1. Find f(1).
questions.hint: The closed dot is on the graph.
questions.solution: 1 ≤ 1 is true, so use x²: f(1) = 1.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² if x ≤ 1; 3 − x if x > 1. Find f(−3).
The left piece ends with an open dot at x = −3 and goes left. The right piece starts with a closed dot at x = −3 and goes right. What is the domain?
questions.hint: Is x = −3 on the graph?
questions.solution: The closed dot at x = −3 is on the graph. Left of −3 and right of −3 are covered too. The domain is all real numbers.

questions.prompt: The left piece ends with an open dot at x = 2. The right piece starts with an open dot at x = 2. What is the domain?
questions.hint: Is there a point on the graph at x = 2?
questions.solution: Both ends at x = 2 are open dots, so no point on the graph has x = 2. The domain is all real numbers except 2.

questions.prompt: For x ≤ 2, a piece is a line through (0, 1) and (2, 5). What is its y-value when x = −3?
questions.hint: Slope = (5 − 1)/(2 − 0). The y-intercept is 1.
questions.solution: The slope is 4/2 = 2, so the line is y = 2x + 1. At x = −3: y = 2(−3) + 1 = −5.

questions.prompt: A piece starts at x = 4 and goes right, with an open dot at x = 4. Which condition describes it?
questions.hint: Open dot means the endpoint is not included.
questions.solution: An open dot means 4 is not included, and the piece goes right. So the condition is x > 4.

teach.title: Absolute value and real situations
text: An absolute value function is a piecewise function: |x| = −x if x < 0, and x if x ≥ 0. For |x − a|, change x to x − a.
Prices that change at a cutoff are piecewise too. Find the rule for the interval your input is in, then plug in.

example.problem: Write |x − 3| as a piecewise function.

questions.prompt: Which piecewise function equals |x − 3|?
questions.hint: The expression inside is negative when x < 3.
questions.solution: When x < 3, x − 3 is negative, so |x − 3| = −(x − 3). When x ≥ 3 it is x − 3.

questions.prompt: Use |x − 3| = −(x − 3) for x < 3 and x − 3 for x ≥ 3. What is the value at x = −1?
A garage charges $4 for up to 2 hours. After 2 hours the cost is c(t) = 3t − 2. How much does 5 hours cost?
questions.hint: 5 hours is more than 2 hours.
questions.solution: Use 3t − 2: c(5) = 15 − 2 = 13. The cost is $13.

questions.prompt: The garage in the last question charges $4 for 0 < t ≤ 2. How much does 1.5 hours cost?
questions.hint: Which interval is 1.5 in?
questions.solution: 1.5 ≤ 2, so the flat rate applies. The cost is $4.

questions.prompt: The garage cost for more than 2 hours is c(t) = 3t − 2. For how many hours is the cost $19?
questions.hint: Solve 3t − 2 = 19.
questions.solution: 3t = 21, so t = 7. Check: 7 > 2, so the rule applies.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x + 5 if x ≤ 1; 3x if x > 1. A student says f(1) = 3. What was the mistake?
choices: Used x + 5, but f(1) = 3 is correct
Used 3x, but 1 is not greater than 1; f(1) = 6
Used x + 5 but forgot the 5; f(1) = 1
questions.hint: Which condition includes 1?
questions.solution: x ≤ 1 includes 1, so use x + 5: f(1) = 6. The rule 3x needs x > 1.

questions.hint: Find each value with the right rule, then add.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 if x < 3; x + c if x ≥ 3. For what value of c do the pieces meet at x = 3, with no gap?
questions.hint: Find the first rule at x = 3. Make the second rule match.
questions.solution: First rule at x = 3: 2 · 3 + 1 = 7. Second rule: 3 + c. Set 3 + c = 7, so c = 4.

questions.prompt: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x + 7)?
questions.hint: The number under the root cannot be negative. Solve x + 7 ≥ 0.
questions.solution: x + 7 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ −7. The square root is defined at 0, so −7 is included: [−7, ∞).

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = 2x² − 18.
questions.hint: Set y = 0 and solve for x².
questions.solution: 2x² = 18, so x² = 9 and x = ±3.

questions.prompt: On which interval is the graph of f decreasing?
questions.hint: Decreasing means the graph goes down as you move right. Look between the high point and the low point.
questions.solution: The graph rises to a local maximum at x = 1, falls to a local minimum at x = 3, then rises. So f is decreasing on (1, 3).

questions.prompt: What is the end behavior of f(x) = −2x³ + x?
choices: As x → ∞, f(x) → ∞, and as x → −∞, f(x) → −∞
As x → ∞, f(x) → −∞, and as x → −∞, f(x) → ∞
As x → ∞, f(x) → ∞, and as x → −∞, f(x) → ∞
As x → ∞, f(x) → −∞, and as x → −∞, f(x) → −∞
questions.hint: The leading term decides. Odd degree with a negative leading coefficient.
questions.solution: The leading term is −2x³. For large positive x it is very negative. For large negative x it is very positive.

questions.prompt: A table has x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and y = 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4. Which parent function fits?
questions.hint: Each time x goes up by 1, what happens to y?
questions.solution: y doubles every time x increases by 1, and y = 1 at x = 0. That is y = 2ˣ.

questions.prompt: Which parent function is shown?
questions.hint: It passes through (−8, −2), (0, 0) and (8, 2), and it is steepest at the origin.
questions.solution: The curve is defined for negative x too and passes through (−8, −2), (0, 0), (8, 2). That is y = ∛x.

questions.prompt: Which parent function is odd (symmetric about the origin)?
questions.hint: An odd function satisfies f(−x) = −f(x).
questions.solution: (−x)³ = −x³, so y = x³ is odd. x² and |x| are even. √x is not defined for negative x, so it is neither.

questions.prompt: The point (−1, 4) is on f. Which point is on g(x) = f(x − 6) + 2?
questions.hint: Right 6 adds 6 to x. Up 2 adds 2 to y.

questions.prompt: f(4) = 10. If g(x) = f(x + 3) − 7, what is g(1)?
questions.hint: Find which input of f you need: x + 3 when x = 1.

questions.prompt: The point (−3, 5) is on f. The point (k, 5) is on g(x) = f(−x). What is k?
questions.hint: Reflecting over the y-axis changes the sign of the x-value.
questions.solution: g(3) = f(−3) = 5, so the point (3, 5) is on g. k = 3.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² + 4x and g(x) = f(−x). What is g(3)?
The point (2, −3) is on f. The point (k, −3) is on g(x) = f(x/4). What is k?
questions.hint: x/4 means b = 1/4. Divide the x-value by 1/4.
Multiply the output by −5.

questions.prompt: The point (−2, 3) is on f. What is the y-coordinate of its image on g(x) = −2f(x − 1) + 5?
questions.hint: Multiply the y-value by −2 first, then add 5.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² and g(x) = 3f(x + 2) − 10. What is g(1)?
questions.hint: x + 2 = 3 when x = 1.

questions.prompt: Which describes g(x) = ½f(x + 4) − 3?
choices: Right 4, vertical compression by ½, down 3
Left 4, horizontal compression by ½, down 3
Left 4, vertical compression by ½, down 3
questions.hint: Inside the parentheses, x + 4 moves left. The ½ is outside f.
questions.solution: x + 4 shifts left 4. The ½ multiplies outputs: vertical compression by ½. − 3 shifts down 3.

questions.prompt: This graph starts at one point and heads down and right. It comes from f(x) = √x. Which is its equation?
questions.hint: The start point is (−1, 3), and the graph goes down from there.
questions.solution: The start point (−1, 3) gives h = −1 and k = 3. At x = 3 the graph is at y = −1: a · 2 + 3 = −1, so a = −2.

questions.prompt: A parabola with vertex (−2, −6) passes through (0, 2). Its equation is y = a(x + 2)² − 6. What is a?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 0 and y = 2.

questions.prompt: What is the vertex of y = −3|x − 8| + 1?
questions.hint: The vertex is (h, k) in y = a|x − h| + k.
questions.solution: x − 8 gives h = 8, and + 1 gives k = 1. The vertex is (8, 1).

questions.prompt: Find the x-intercepts of y = ½|x − 5| − 3.
questions.hint: Get |x − 5| alone: add 3, then multiply by 2.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the left side of y = −4|x + 1| + 9?
questions.hint: The left side has slope −a.
questions.solution: a = −4, so the left side has slope −a = 4.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 3x − 5 if x < −1; x² + 2 if x ≥ −1. Find f(−1).
questions.hint: Which condition includes −1?
questions.solution: x ≥ −1 includes −1, so use x² + 2: f(−1) = 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.prompt: Shipping costs s(w) = 6 dollars if 0 < w ≤ 2, and s(w) = 6 + 1.5(w − 2) dollars if w > 2, where w is the weight in pounds. What does it cost to ship 6 pounds?
questions.hint: 6 is more than 2, so use the second rule.

questions.prompt: p(x) = x² − 1 if x < 3; 2x + 5 if x > 3. What is the domain of p?
questions.hint: Is x = 3 in either condition?
questions.solution: x = 3 is neither less than 3 nor greater than 3, so no rule covers it. The domain is all real numbers except 3.
